To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of chronic ethanol on [14C]-2-deoxyglucose (2-DG) uptake by the brain is complex.
chronic alcohol consumption causes increased deoxyglucose metabolism in the rat brain, especially in the limbic system.
the effect of chronic ethanol exposure on the metabolism of the rat brain is to cause an increase in the regional cerebral utilization of glucose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic ethanol consumption and withdrawal on the metabolism of brain tissue.
the effect of alcohol on brain function.
the effects of chronic alcoholism on the human brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ethanol consumption in the rat causes a significant increase in the uptake of [14 C]deoxygluceose by the brain, and that this increase in uptake is not due to the effects of ethanol on the blood-brain barrier.
chronic ethanol treatment of rats causes an increase in deoxy glucose uptake in brain with the limbic system most affected.
chronic ethanol ingestion in rats leads to an increase of deoxyglucose utilization in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethanol consumption results in a general increase in deoxy-glucose uptake in the brain.
chronic alcohol consumption leads to increased deoxyglucose metabolism, particularly in the limbic system.
chronic alcoholism causes an increased rate of glucose utilization in the rat brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of chronic ethanol exposure on the brain are widespread.
the brain is a very sensitive organ and is affected by even moderate alcohol consumption.
there is no single region of the brain that is responsible for the effects of alcohol on behavior.
